posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Challenge Omnitron vs. Omnitron-U, The Adamant Sentinels, and Chrono-Ranger in Madame Mittermeier's.

Fairly easy Mint for me. I probably dragged the game out a little beyond what I needed to by using damage reduction from Idealist and Chrono-Ranger, but it worked out pretty well. It made the Flechettes round hurt a lot less.

MMFFCC was fairly helpful, it did plenty of damage to Omnitron and sometimes helped me get Adaptive Plating reset back to a type I wanted. I saw and left out both copies of Adaptive Plating, there's plenty of damage types to go around here.

I won the round after I saw the All-Seeing, who helped me get a couple extra card plays out of the Sentinels.

Imagine this one will turn different quickly based on how one uses Chrono-Ranger's environment destruction.

Final HP: Omnitron-U 12, Sentinels 3/3/3/9, Chrono-Ranger 11.

posts.name: GainzofCastamere
posts.cooked:
Mint for me. I was sad to see my equipment get wiped so early and was a little concerned when I lost Wraith and Medico. But, once All-Seeing popped up and it hit me that he would combo well with the with the Sentinels one-shot heavy deck, the match improved a great deal and brought the fallen Sentinels back. Also got to use Omnitron-X's Self-Sabotage to blow up some of villainous Omnitron's components. Love it when I can do that.

 

 Omintron ended up being taken out by a You Won't Believe Your Eyes! being comboed with Chrono-Ranger's Ultimate Target + base power.  

 

Final HP: Omnitron-U 6, Sentinels 6/6/2/5, CR- 3.

posts.name: scifantasy
posts.cooked:
Mint, but not quite as easy as others. I ended up getting more hurt by the double Unstable Midway into You Won't Believe..., and focused some Temporal Grenades and Terraforming Beam into cleaning up the circus. Omnitron itself was a breeze--the Challenge mode made no difference as there were never multiple Components on the table, and the few Drones that came out not only got wrecked in short order but got recycled thanks to Adamant Wraith.

 

The worst play of the game was Omnitron's, though. Sedative Flechettes: tore straight through my Ongoing-based setups. I was worried there, but managed to pull it out. Everyone in single digits, but alive.

posts.name: Arthur_Wynne
posts.cooked: Mint, everyone at 9-11 HP. Very fun game, but not as difficult as I thought it would be. Never really in danger at any point, even Sedative Flechettes was just annoying. I also left out the Reactive Plating, the Sentinels use so many different damage types that it's basically irrelevant. Madame Mittermeier's is an unpleasant place, but Omnitron's beam power and Chrono-Ranger's grenades kept the most dangerous cards off the table (like Hall of Mirrors, for example.) Omnitron played Terraforming turn 1 on an empty board, but I never saw the second. (It probably got discarded.) The Adamant Sentinels were the work horses here, but Omnitron-U is also quite a pinch hitter.

posts.name: QuirkyDM
posts.cooked:
Straight forward mint. I didn't have the trouble everyone else did. Flechettes came out before I had anyone set up decently. Adaptive Plating stopped Chrono-Ranger a few times, but I got his Neuro-Toxin Dart Thrower out to do Toxic Damage, so it wasn't a big deal. Omnitron-X's Defensive Blast goes right through Adaptive Plating and like others, Writhe cycled all destroyed Drones to the bottom of the deck. There was never more than one component out so Omnitron's challenge mode was not an issue.

The only environment card I destroyed was the Caurosel of Horror and Idealist quickly discarded 2 cards to get rid of Freak Show. When All-Seeing Alzrabar came out, I discard every single turn from whoever had a lot of cards (usually Sentinels or Chrono-Ranger) and played off the Sentinels deck. Along with Sentinel Tactics, the damage came off quickly. I had all of the Sentinels signature cards out as well and when Omnitron was around 50 hp, I started throwing out Bounties.

I never saw Maze of Mirrors or Shooting Gallery. In the end, it was just a lot of smashing and shooting. Everyone was at mint except Chrono-Ranger, who was only down by a few points.

posts.name: FrivYeti
posts.cooked:
Mint, but it was a close one. I got lucky for a while - no Sedative Flechettes or Terraforming ever dropped, which was really good because there were seven or eight cards in the environment deck at any given time and it would have been bad. I made the mistake of dropping Jim's grenades on the first turn to prep, and then Omnitron immediately blew up all my equipment, and then I never saw another Ongoing or Environment kill for the rest of the game. 

By the end, I lost Chrono-Ranger, the Idealist died twice, and the only reason that I survived was that I kept Hippocratic Oath out, and the environment kept forcing Doctor Medico to first hit everyone for 1 damage, and then hit himself for 5 damage, and both of those turned into healing. I was healing roughly 15-20 HP per turn, and at the end of the game everyone was still under 10 HP.
